core_obligations: Set up the localizations (proof lines 1969-1992): the author introduces the morphisms j : C/U -> C and the corresponding functors, and rewrites the restriction map I(U) -> I(U') as the map induced by the monomorphism a.

Construct the extension (proof lines 1995-2009): using that a is a monomorphism, a section over U' is the restriction of a section over U after extending by zero along the inclusion, and injectivity of I supplies the extension, which is exactly the surjectivity of the restriction map.
proof_roadmap: Localise the site at U and U' and express the restriction map through the monomorphism a.
Use the monomorphism hypothesis to extend a section supported on U' to a section over U by zero.
Apply injectivity of I to obtain the required preimage, giving surjectivity.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that for a monomorphism a : U' -> U in a ringed site and an injective module I, the restriction map I(U) -> I(U') is surjective (statement lines 1961-1967). The proof localises the site at U and U' and expresses the restriction map through the functors attached to the monomorphism (proof lines 1969-1992), then extends a section over U' by zero along the monomorphism and applies injectivity of I to produce a preimage (proof lines 1995-2009). The non-formal content is the use of the monomorphism hypothesis to make the extension by zero a subfunctor of the identity, which is what injectivity is applied to. The claim is H2: one adjunction set-up plus one extension argument.
